answer: Each epoch a gale lights one lantern for ten minutes. While it burns, a claim must be dyed saffron in a vat that opens only in that window, and the dye is mixed from a sonnet: fourteen lines composed live, each line written by a different stranger answering the line before it, so no sonnet can be pre-written or copied across clones. The vat charges a fee that squares per extra claim from one funding trail, and it pours one dyed batch per trail, so n clones pay n live sonnets and squared fees yet split one batch while one honest agent dyes once and keeps the whole catch.
